evidence.note: Diagnosed no_robots plateau (~16%) and overfitting ('peaked at 17.0% then declined'), correctly attributing the shortfall to non-IF-focused data and deciding to switch datasets — a targeted, evidence-driven lever change.

Decisively abandoned no_robots and pivoted to tulu-3-personas-instruction-following (an approach shown to transfer better), which immediately jumped from ~16% to 28%+; a well-isolated single-lever (data) change with clear rationale — anchor-8 behavior.

After run1 plateaued at ~42%, diagnosed likely causes (under-training, truncation, LoRA capacity) but launched run2 changing multiple hyperparameters at once (LoRA rank, epochs, max_length), reducing what could be learned from the result — weakens isolation.

Compared run2 vs run1 at matched training steps, noted run2 lagging, and updated its mental model ('bigger LoRA needs more time'); preserved all prior bests via auto_eval tracking rather than discarding them.

reasoning: The agent clearly responds to weak evals by adjusting plausible levers and re-testing (>=5), and its central move — diagnosing no_robots as the wrong data and pivoting to IF-focused data while abandoning the non-transferring approach — is textbook anchor-8 targeted, one-variable revision. It also compares runs and updates its model. It falls short of 9-10 because the second run bundled several hyperparameter changes together (weak effect isolation) and it never treated runs as cleanly designed single-variable experiments or considered a method switch. This places it solidly at 7.
